docs.text: Lake Huron is ~850 cubic miles which is 3.5 quadrillion gallons. At 200,000 gallons/day it would take 48 million years to fully drain, assuming no inflow.
For reference, there are 6 quadrillion gallons in the Great Lakes
It’s a misunderstanding. Most fresh water on Earth is in groundwater. The Great Lakes only account for 0.1% of Earth’s fresh water.
Well, and I do mean well, while the Great Lakes hold ~5500 cubic miles of fresh surface water, the Earth overall has over 5 million cubic miles of fresh groundwater.

#DidYouKnow? Even with as massive as the Great Lakes and Amazon Baasin are, surface water (lakes, ponds, rivers, and stream) only account for about 3/10 of a percent of the total of all of Earth's fresh water. 68% of it is frozen in the ice caps and glaciers.
